findings.title: `queued` default is evaluated once at import time
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a plain default value, so Python evaluates it once when the class is defined. Every `AssignmentSource` created without an explicit `queued` (including every one from `from_integration`) gets the timestamp of process startup, not of the assignment. Any later use of `queued` for ordering, staleness or debouncing would be wrong. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

findings.title: Raw datetime placed in Celery task kwargs; deserialized type is not validated
findings.body: `assignment_source.to_dict()` uses `dataclasses.asdict`, which leaves `queued` as a `datetime` object, and that dict is passed as a Celery task kwarg. With a JSON task serializer this either fails to serialize or arrives on the worker as a string. `AssignmentSource.from_dict` then does `cls(**input_dict)` with no type conversion, so `queued` silently becomes a `str` despite being typed as `datetime`. Serialize `queued` explicitly (e.g. ISO string or epoch) in `to_dict` and parse it back in `from_dict`.

findings.title: New task kwarg is not safe during a rolling deploy
findings.body: Producers now always send `assignment_source_dict` to `sync_assignee_outbound` (even when its value is None). During a rolling deploy, workers still running the old task signature will receive the unexpected kwarg and raise `TypeError`, so assignee syncs fail until every worker is updated. The usual pattern is to deploy the task parameter first and start sending it in a follow-up change.

findings.title: New `assignment_source` kwarg passed to every integration's `sync_assignee_outbound`
findings.body: The task now calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=...)` on every provider. Any concrete implementation (Jira, Jira Server, VSTS, GitHub, example, etc.) whose override lacks `**kwargs` will raise `TypeError`, and outbound assignee sync will break for that provider. Confirm that all overrides accept the kwarg, or add it to their signatures.

findings.title: `sync_status_outbound` gains `assignment_source` but nothing passes it
findings.body: The abstract `sync_status_outbound` signature now accepts `assignment_source`, but no caller provides it and status sync does not go through `should_sync` with a source. The same inbound-to-outbound cycle for status changes is therefore not prevented, while the signature implies it is. Either wire the source through the status sync path or drop the unused parameter.

findings.title: No end-to-end test that inbound sync suppresses outbound to the same integration
findings.body: The new test calls `GroupAssignee.objects.assign` directly with an `AssignmentSource`. Nothing exercises `sync_group_assignee_inbound` (assign or deassign) to check that it no longer triggers `sync_assignee_outbound` for the originating integration, which is the cycle this PR is meant to break. There is also no `to_dict`/`from_dict` round-trip test through the task, which would have exposed the datetime serialization problem.
